name: CI
display_title: Avoid redundant analysis and RBE downloads in CI

head_commit.message:
Avoid redundant analysis and RBE downloads in CI

In `build_tools/ci/build.py` we used to run a separate `bazel build --nobuild` step before the actual `bazel build` or `bazel test` invocation to retry repository fetches. This added a second target-analysis pass (~5-30s on most builds, and ~2.5 min on `Hermetic ROCm` where `+rocm_configure_ext` re-evaluated the main repo mapping) plus BES upload overhead.

Instead let's configure `--experimental_repository_downloader_retries=5` in `tensorflow.bazelrc` so Bazel retries transient download errors in-process without a second invocation, and remove `bazel build --nobuild` from `build_tools/ci/build.py`.

Also:

1. Switch `common:rbe_base` in `tensorflow.bazelrc` (and the Linux JAX RBE builds in `build_tools/ci/build.py`) to `--remote_download_minimal` and `--nobuild_runfile_links` so CI shards still compile and link all non-test binaries on RBE without downloading them or materializing runfiles symlink trees when they are not executed locally.
2. Keep `--remote_download_toplevel` and `--build_runfile_links` enabled for the benchmark presubmit builds (which execute the built binaries from `bazel-bin`) and `--remote_download_toplevel` for `clang-tidy-common` (which reads the generated `.clang-tidy.yaml` files from disk).

Comparing full builds with a warm RBE cache (https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50787 vs. https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51241), this reduces `Run build.py` times across RBE jobs:

- `XLA Linux x86 GPU Hermetic ROCm` (always full build): 11m 49s -> 6m 08s (-2m 38s from removing `--nobuild`, -2m 59s in execution/download phase)
- `XLA Linux X86 GPU ONEAPI` (always full build): 4m 36s -> 3m 49s (-43s in execution/download phase)
- `JAX Linux x86 GPU T4` (always full build): 2m 27s -> 2m 09s (-16s in execution/download phase)
- `XLA Linux x86 CPU WORKSPACE` (full build, warm RBE cache): 7m 54s -> 2m 22s (execution/download phase drops from 6m 27s to 59s; 3,811 fewer `.runfiles` actions)
- `XLA Linux x86 GPU T4` (full build, warm RBE cache): 7m 53s -> 3m 41s (execution/download phase drops from 5m 35s to 1m 08s; 3,029 fewer `.runfiles` actions)

display_title: Preserve `stack_frame_index` when embedding computations in `XlaBuilder`.

head_commit.message:
Preserve `stack_frame_index` when embedding computations in `XlaBuilder`.

`XlaBuilder::AddSubComputation` copied the embedded computation's
`HloComputationProto`s but dropped its `stack_frame_index`, leaving the
instructions' `stack_frame_id`s dangling. `HloModule::CanonicalizeStackFrameIds`
then reset them to 0, so source locations were lost for any computation built
via `ConvertMlirHloToHlo` and then embedded through `xla::Call`.

`XlaBuilder` now keeps a `StackFrames` table for imported computations:

-   `AddSubComputation` re-interns each imported frame (and its parent chain)
    into it, so identical frames are stored once, and rewrites the imported
    instructions' ids accordingly.
-   `BuildSubComputation` re-interns a child builder's table into its parent, only for entries that were imported with a stack frame index.
-   `Build()` / `BuildConstantSubGraph()` emit it as the module's
    `stack_frame_index`.
-   Ids set directly via `SetOpMetadata` (i.e. on the builder's own
    instructions, or on imported computations that carry no table) refer to a
    caller-owned table and are left untouched.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1000279666

name: CI
display_title: Allow in place buffer sharing through kCopyDone in HeapSimulator

head_commit.message:
Allow in place buffer sharing through kCopyDone in HeapSimulator

In HloDataflowAnalysis, kCopyDone forwards the HloValue defined at kCopyStart
index {0}. When DecreasingSizeRunsHeap checks whether an instruction can share
its operand buffer in place, it tests whether the instruction is a direct user
of the HloValue's defining instruction. Because a consumer of kCopyDone has
kCopyDone as its operand rather than kCopyStart, in place buffer sharing never
fired across asynchronous copies and forced two disjoint buffers to remain
simultaneously live.

Recognize operands that are a kCopyDone of the defining kCopyStart{0} value and
pass the kCopyDone instruction to CanShareOperandBufferWithUser so elementwise
and fusion consumers can reuse the destination buffer of an asynchronous copy in
place.

Tests:
- //third_party/tensorflow/compiler/xla/service/heap_simulator:heap_simulator_test
PiperOrigin-RevId: 1004542530

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Strength-reduce one-hot dots into gather and select.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Strength-reduce one-hot dots into gather and select.

Multiplying a one-hot matrix by a weight table `W` is just a row lookup.
Rewrite it as a gather + select. For now its turned off by default. The numbers in the CL are taken with the child CL which turns it on by default. This is just to keep rollback churn low. I want to have it unconditionally later.

Also:
- If the weight is a `reshape(broadcast(param))` on non-contracting
  dimensions (e.g. broadcasting `param[256, 16, 512]` to `[256, 65536]`),
  gather first and apply the `broadcast` + `reshape` afterward so we don't
  gather 8x the data.
- Skip F32 dots with default (TF32) precision so TF32 GEMM numerics do not
  change.
PiperOrigin-RevId: 1003843503

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add ScanRewriterTriton to the GPU compiler pipeline behind a flag.

head_commit.message:
Add the debug option `xla_gpu_experimental_enable_triton_scan` (default off). When it is set, `GpuCompiler` runs `ScanRewriterTriton` before `AssociativeScanRewriter`, so eligible associative `kScan` instructions become Triton scan fusions instead of reduce-window trees.

The rewriter only sets the fusion kind to `__triton`; the tiling is chosen later by `PriorityFusion`, `FusionBlockLevelRewriter` or the autotuner.

Eligible scans have rank 1 or 2 with the scan dimension last, and the rewriter does nothing on GPUs that Triton does not support. A tiled scan computes one row per block, so scans with a dimension of at least 32768 also need at least 64 rows (`kMinParallelElements`); otherwise the hierarchical scan of `AssociativeScanRewriter` is faster (crossover at 64 rows on H100 and 32 on B200). Shorter scans are faster with Triton at any batch size.

For a cumsum with an elementwise epilogue on f32[B, N], with B from 1 to 256 and N from 1024 to 262144, enabling the flag is never slower on H100 and B200. It is 1.05–2.9x (H100) and 1.06–2.8x (B200) faster for N < 32768, and up to 1.9x (H100) and 2.3x (B200) faster for N ≥ 32768 and B ≥ 64.

A top-p sampling mask (softmax, cumsum, compare and select) on f32[B, K] with B from 1 to 256 and K in {64, 128} compiles to a single Triton kernel: 1.3–1.5 µs instead of 3.3–4.5 µs on H100, and 2.5–3.1 µs instead of 5.9–8.4 µs on B200.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 982293610

display_title: Fix base dilation overlap in SpaceToBatchConverter

head_commit.message:
Fix base dilation overlap in SpaceToBatchConverter

When inherent_low_padding equals base_dilation_factor, SpaceToBatchConverter prepends one undilated element to each split and sets low_padding_for_conv to 0.

For each split of S undilated elements to produce S * base_dilation_factor outputs, the high-side overlap must be kernel_spatial_dim_size + base_dilation_factor - 2 rather than kernel_spatial_dim_size (which only matched for base_dilation_factor == 2). Therefore this change updates last_overlap in GetConvolutionDetails accordingly.

Fixes https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/51365

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1004178625

head_commit.message:
PR #51324: Bump numpy from 2.4.6 to 2.5.4 Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51324 Bumps [numpy](https://github.com/numpy/numpy) from 2.4.6 to 2.5.4.
Release notes

Sourced from numpy's releases.

v2.5.4 (Oct 10, 2026)

NumPy 2.5.4 Release Notes

Released on 2026-10-10.

NumPy 2.5.4 is a patch release that fixes bugs discovered after the 2.5.3 release. Highlights are:

  • Many typing fixes and improvements,
  • A workaround for the MSVC 19.51 bug, see below.

This release supports Python versions 3.12-3.15.

Improvements

  • numpy.linalg.svd and numpy.linalg.lstsq now raise for inputs containing infinities instead of returning garbage results.

  • Fixed hangs in numpy.linalg.svd and numpy.linalg.lstsq for certain inputs containing infinities for recent versions of some LAPACK implementations.

  • numpy.linalg.cond now handles non-finite inputs more consistently.

(gh-32593)

StringDType hashing with NaN sentinels

StringDType instances with equivalent floating-point NaN sentinels now have equal hashes. Previously, distinct NaN objects could produce equal dtype instances with different hashes, causing dictionary lookups and set deduplication to fail.

(gh-32563)

Changes

MaskedArray resets a fill_value that cannot be represented in a new dtype

A fill_value copied from a source array is now reset to the default fill_value for the new dtype when it cannot be represented in that dtype. Previously the copied value could be stale: ufuncs that change dtype left the result holding a fill_value typed for the old dtype, which raised a TypeError only when something later validated it (such as .view()), and a floating point fill_value that overflows an integer dtype was kept as an out-of-range value together with a RuntimeWarning. Both now fall back to the default, including when a masked array is passed to MaskedArray with a different dtype. A fill_value given explicitly by the user is still validated and raises as before. This can now raise a ComplexWarning if the fill_value is complex and the new dtype is real.

v2.5.4 (Oct 10, 2026)

NumPy 2.5.4 Release Notes

Released on 2026-10-10.

NumPy 2.5.4 is a patch release that fixes bugs discovered after the 2.5.3 release. Highlights are:

  • Many typing fixes and improvements,
  • A workaround for the MSVC 19.51 bug, see below.

This release supports Python versions 3.12-3.15.

Improvements

  • numpy.linalg.svd and numpy.linalg.lstsq now raise for inputs containing infinities instead of returning garbage results.

  • Fixed hangs in numpy.linalg.svd and numpy.linalg.lstsq for certain inputs containing infinities for recent versions of some LAPACK implementations.

  • numpy.linalg.cond now handles non-finite inputs more consistently.

(gh-32593)

StringDType hashing with NaN sentinels

StringDType instances with equivalent floating-point NaN sentinels now have equal hashes. Previously, distinct NaN objects could produce equal dtype instances with different hashes, causing dictionary lookups and set deduplication to fail.

(gh-32563)

Changes

MaskedArray resets a fill_value that cannot be represented in a new dtype

A fill_value copied from a source array is now reset to the default fill_value for the new dtype when it cannot be represented in that dtype. Previously the copied value could be stale: ufuncs that change dtype left the result holding a fill_value typed for the old dtype, which raised a TypeError only when something later validated it (such as .view()), and a floating point fill_value that overflows an integer dtype was kept as an out-of-range value together with a RuntimeWarning. Both now fall back to the default, including when a masked array is passed to MaskedArray with a different dtype. A fill_value given explicitly by the user is still validated and raises as before. This can now raise a ComplexWarning if the fill_value is complex and the new dtype is real.

[XLA:GPU] Disable warmup and init updates for symmetric-memory RaggedAllToAllThunk commands.

When RaggedAllToAllThunk uses the symmetric-memory kernel, it records explicit command buffer launch nodes instead of tracing a stream, so it does not require warmup or command buffer updates on initialization.

name: CI
display_title: Avoid redundant analysis and RBE downloads in CI

head_commit.message:
Avoid redundant analysis and RBE downloads in CI

In `build_tools/ci/build.py` we used to run a separate `bazel build --nobuild` step before the actual `bazel build` or `bazel test` invocation to retry repository fetches. This added a second target-analysis pass (~5-30s on most builds, and ~2.5 min on `Hermetic ROCm` where `+rocm_configure_ext` re-evaluated the main repo mapping) plus BES upload overhead.

Instead let's configure `--experimental_repository_downloader_retries=5` in `tensorflow.bazelrc` so Bazel retries transient download errors in-process without a second invocation, and remove `bazel build --nobuild` from `build_tools/ci/build.py`.

Also:

1. Switch `common:rbe_base` in `tensorflow.bazelrc` (and the Linux JAX RBE builds in `build_tools/ci/build.py`) to `--remote_download_minimal` and `--nobuild_runfile_links` so CI shards still compile and link all non-test binaries on RBE without downloading them or materializing runfiles symlink trees when they are not executed locally.
2. Keep `--remote_download_toplevel` and `--build_runfile_links` enabled for the benchmark presubmit builds (which execute the built binaries from `bazel-bin`) and `--remote_download_toplevel` for `clang-tidy-common` (which reads the generated `.clang-tidy.yaml` files from disk).

Comparing full builds with a warm RBE cache (https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50787 vs. https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51241), this reduces `Run build.py` times across RBE jobs:

- `XLA Linux x86 GPU Hermetic ROCm` (always full build): 11m 49s -> 6m 08s (-2m 38s from removing `--nobuild`, -2m 59s in execution/download phase)
- `XLA Linux X86 GPU ONEAPI` (always full build): 4m 36s -> 3m 49s (-43s in execution/download phase)
- `JAX Linux x86 GPU T4` (always full build): 2m 27s -> 2m 09s (-16s in execution/download phase)
- `XLA Linux x86 CPU WORKSPACE` (full build, warm RBE cache): 7m 54s -> 2m 22s (execution/download phase drops from 6m 27s to 59s; 3,811 fewer `.runfiles` actions)
- `XLA Linux x86 GPU T4` (full build, warm RBE cache): 7m 53s -> 3m 41s (execution/download phase drops from 5m 35s to 1m 08s; 3,029 fewer `.runfiles` actions)

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1003110623

display_title: PR #49450: [ROCm] Autotune the MFMA instruction size for Triton GEMMs

head_commit.message:
PR #49450: [ROCm] Autotune the MFMA instruction size for Triton GEMMs

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/49450

📝 Summary of Changes
Add `mfma_size` to the Triton GEMM config and autotune it on MFMA targets. MI300 default configs get `mfma_size: 16` variants. MI350 tries them only in exhaustive search.

🎯 Justification
The auto MFMA choice is often not the fastest on MI300.

🚀 Kind of Contribution:⚡️ Performance Improvement,

📊 Benchmark
  - MI300 wins: GPT-J 6B -12.9%, Flan-T5-L -9.7%, SDXL -6.5%, PaliGemma -5.5%.
Copybara import of the project:

--
263756c5777de795be80295c670e6b53a487dd56 by Aleksei Nurmukhametov <anurmukh@amd.com>:

[ROCm] Autotune the MFMA instruction size for Triton GEMMs

Triton picks the largest MFMA that fits the tile, which is not always
the fastest. Let the autotuner also try 16x16 MFMAs so it can pick
whichever is faster.

Tried by default on MI300 only. On MI350, it is limited to exhaustive
search. WMMA targets don't use MFMA.

Merging this change closes #49450

display_title: Enhance `tsl::profiler::MergeXSpace` with pointer overload and arena-aware ownership transfer.

head_commit.message:
Enhance `tsl::profiler::MergeXSpace` with pointer overload and arena-aware ownership transfer.

- Adds pointer overload `void MergeXSpace(XSpace* from, XSpace* to)` supporting both arena-allocated (`UnsafeArenaReleaseLast` / `UnsafeArenaAddAllocated`) and heap-allocated `XSpace` instances.
- Preserves plane and line insertion order using reverse iterator traversal during chunk transfers.
- Preserves `XLine` `name` and `display_name` when merging into an existing line with empty name/display_name.
- Adds unit tests covering pointer-based merging, arena transfers, and order/name preservation.

display_title: PR #50583: [ROCm] [CUDA] Serve pinned_host buffers from host memory with the VMM allocator PR 3/3

head_commit.message:
PR #50583: [ROCm] [CUDA] Serve pinned_host buffers from host memory with the VMM allocator PR 3/3

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50583

Note on these PR chains:  diff here shows +877 lines because it has other two commits combined here , once those two PRs go in actual diff here is only +284. also all three PRs touch shared XLA GPU code.

## 📝 Summary of Changes

With the VMM allocator (`GpuAllocatorConfig::Kind::kVmm`), `pinned_host` buffers now come from pinned host memory instead of device memory, on CUDA and ROCm.

- The PJRT GPU client passes the VMM allocator the same per-device pinned host allocators the BFC path uses. It creates the allocator through the generic `DeviceAddressVmmAllocator::Create()`, so there are no CUDA/ROCm `#if` branches.
- Without a host allocator, `MemorySpace::kHost` requests now fail with `FailedPrecondition` instead of silently getting device memory.

Part 3 of 3; needs both:
1. https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50581: VA remapping skips host memory space allocations
2. https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50582: the VMM allocator serves `MemorySpace::kHost` from a host allocator
3. This PR. **Until PR 1 and PR 2 land, this branch also has their commits; only the last commit is new.**

## 🎯 Justification

For `kVmm`, nothing served the host memory space, so `pinned_host` buffers got device memory with no CPU mapping and any CPU access segfaulted. Orbax checkpointing does exactly that, so every JAX job with `XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_ALLOCATOR=vmm` crashed at its first checkpoint save, on CUDA and ROCm. Command buffer update modes other than `ALWAYS_UPDATE` force the VMM allocator, so they crashed too.

VMM clients now behave like BFC clients for `pinned_host`: the same host memory limit (`XLA_PJRT_GPU_HOST_MEMORY_LIMIT_GB`) and preallocation setting apply, and host offloading actually moves data to host memory.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix, 🧪 Tests

## 🧪 Unit Tests

- `se_gpu_pjrt_client_test`: with VMM, a `pinned_host` buffer created from host data and a `pinned_host` program output are readable on the CPU.
- `se_gpu_pjrt_client_multi_gpu_test`: `pinned_host` buffers on two devices are readable on the CPU.
- `device_address_vmm_allocator_test`: `kHost` without a host allocator fails.

PR #51324: Bump numpy from 2.4.6 to 2.5.4 Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51324 Bumps [numpy](https://github.com/numpy/numpy) from 2.4.6 to 2.5.4.
Release notes

Sourced from numpy's releases.

v2.5.4 (Oct 10, 2026)

NumPy 2.5.4 Release Notes

Released on 2026-10-10.

NumPy 2.5.4 is a patch release that fixes bugs discovered after the 2.5.3 release. Highlights are:

  • Many typing fixes and improvements,
  • A workaround for the MSVC 19.51 bug, see below.

This release supports Python versions 3.12-3.15.

Improvements

  • numpy.linalg.svd and numpy.linalg.lstsq now raise for inputs containing infinities instead of returning garbage results.

  • Fixed hangs in numpy.linalg.svd and numpy.linalg.lstsq for certain inputs containing infinities for recent versions of some LAPACK implementations.

  • numpy.linalg.cond now handles non-finite inputs more consistently.

(gh-32593)

StringDType hashing with NaN sentinels

StringDType instances with equivalent floating-point NaN sentinels now have equal hashes. Previously, distinct NaN objects could produce equal dtype instances with different hashes, causing dictionary lookups and set deduplication to fail.

(gh-32563)

Changes

MaskedArray resets a fill_value that cannot be represented in a new dtype

A fill_value copied from a source array is now reset to the default fill_value for the new dtype when it cannot be represented in that dtype. Previously the copied value could be stale: ufuncs that change dtype left the result holding a fill_value typed for the old dtype, which raised a TypeError only when something later validated it (such as .view()), and a floating point fill_value that overflows an integer dtype was kept as an out-of-range value together with a RuntimeWarning. Both now fall back to the default, including when a masked array is passed to MaskedArray with a different dtype. A fill_value given explicitly by the user is still validated and raises as before. This can now raise a ComplexWarning if the fill_value is complex and the new dtype is real.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add ScanRewriterTriton to the GPU compiler pipeline behind a flag.

head_commit.message:
Add the debug option `xla_gpu_experimental_enable_triton_scan` (default off). When it is set, `GpuCompiler` runs `ScanRewriterTriton` before `AssociativeScanRewriter`, so eligible associative `kScan` instructions become Triton scan fusions instead of reduce-window trees.

The rewriter only sets the fusion kind to `__triton`; the tiling is chosen later by `PriorityFusion`, `FusionBlockLevelRewriter` or the autotuner.

Eligible scans have rank 1 or 2 with the scan dimension last, and the rewriter does nothing on GPUs that Triton does not support. A tiled scan computes one row per block, so scans with a dimension of at least 32768 also need at least 64 rows (`kMinParallelElements`); otherwise the hierarchical scan of `AssociativeScanRewriter` is faster (crossover at 64 rows on H100 and 32 on B200). Shorter scans are faster with Triton at any batch size.

For a cumsum with an elementwise epilogue on f32[B, N], with B from 1 to 256 and N from 1024 to 262144, enabling the flag is never slower on H100 and B200. It is 1.05–2.9x (H100) and 1.06–2.8x (B200) faster for N < 32768, and up to 1.9x (H100) and 2.3x (B200) faster for N ≥ 32768 and B ≥ 64.

A top-p sampling mask (softmax, cumsum, compare and select) on f32[B, K] with B from 1 to 256 and K in {64, 128} compiles to a single Triton kernel: 1.3–1.5 µs instead of 3.3–4.5 µs on H100, and 2.5–3.1 µs instead of 5.9–8.4 µs on B200.

display_title: Fix base dilation overlap in SpaceToBatchConverter

head_commit.message:
Fix base dilation overlap in SpaceToBatchConverter

When inherent_low_padding equals base_dilation_factor, SpaceToBatchConverter prepends one undilated element to each split and sets low_padding_for_conv to 0.

For each split of S undilated elements to produce S * base_dilation_factor outputs, the high-side overlap must be kernel_spatial_dim_size + base_dilation_factor - 2 rather than kernel_spatial_dim_size (which only matched for base_dilation_factor == 2). Therefore this change updates last_overlap in GetConvolutionDetails accordingly.

Fixes https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/51365

display_title: Speed up Clang-Tidy, DWYU, and query CI workflows

head_commit.message:
Speed up Clang-Tidy, DWYU, and query CI workflows

The Clang-Tidy, DWYU, and Bazel query/lint workflows in GitHub Actions currently repeat full-repository analysis or do unnecessary work on every pull request:

1. In `clang_tidy.yml` and `run_clang_tidy.sh`, the workflow invokes `./configure.py` (which is meant for local developer setups rather than CI) and writes `build:cuda` and `test --test_env` flags into `xla_configure.bazelrc` that cause `bazel build` to discard the `bazel cquery` analysis cache. In addition, `xla_test` expands into up to 10 backend `cc_test` variants that compile the same sources, non-test `ClangTidy` actions sent to RBE spend ~60s per action uploading `@llvm20_linux_x86_64//:all` and run slower on 1-vCPU RBE workers than on the 16-vCPU runner VM, and `bazel run //build_tools/ci:clang_tidy_diff` triggers a third Bazel invocation even when `--fix` is not set.
2. In `dwyu.yml`, the workflow fetches all branches (`fetch-depth: 0`) and runs `bazelisk build --nobuild //xla/...` across all XLA packages before running `check_dwyu.py` to see whether any C++ targets were modified.
3. In `bazel_dependency_violations.yml`, `bazel_query.yml`, and `bazel_tags.yml`, each job runs `bazel build --nobuild //xla/...` before running `bazel cquery` or `bazel query //xla/...`, which analyzes the entire repository a second time (or runs full configured-target analysis when `bazel query` only needs package loading).

Therefore this change:

1. Replaces `./configure.py` in `clang_tidy.yml` with the fixed `--config rbe_linux_cpu --config cuda_nvcc --config nonccl` configs (passed via a new `--config` flag on `run_clang_tidy.sh` to both `bazel cquery` and `bazel build`), deduplicates `xla_test` backend variants in `run_clang_tidy.sh`, sets `--strategy=ClangTidy=local` so `ClangTidy` aspect actions run directly on the 16-vCPU runner VM while keeping prerequisite build actions on RBE cache, and runs `clang_tidy_diff.py` directly with `python3` when `--fix` is not enabled.
2. Checks out with `fetch-depth: 100` in `dwyu.yml`, runs `check_dwyu.py` before installing `bant` (with SHA-256 verification) or `bazelisk` so PRs without modified C++ targets exit immediately, and scopes `bazelisk build --nobuild` to the packages of the modified targets rather than `//xla/...`.
3. Removes the redundant `bazel build --nobuild //xla/...` step from `bazel_dependency_violations.yml`, `bazel_query.yml`, and `bazel_tags.yml` (downloader retries are already handled by `--experimental_repository_downloader_retries=5`), and skips the `bazel cquery` step in `bazel_dependency_violations.yml` on PRs that do not touch `BUILD`, `.bzl`, `WORKSPACE`, `MODULE.bazel`, or `.bazelrc` files.

Measured wall-clock job durations on PR #51376 (no C++ changes) and PR #51377 (modifying the same two C++ files as PR #50787: `xla/backends/gpu/autotuner/triton/dot_search_space.cc` and `xla/backends/gpu/codegen/triton/tests/scaled_dot_device_test.cc`) compared to PR #50787 and PR #51241:

- `Clang Tidy`:
  - 2-file C++ change (PR #51377 vs. PR #50787): **8m04s** (down from **15m32s**, **48% faster**). `bazel build` reuses the `cquery` analysis cache (analyzing in 0.8s-4.6s instead of 87s), deduplicates `scaled_dot_device_test` variants from 3 targets to 1, runs `ClangTidy` locally without the ~60s RBE upload stall, and runs `clang_tidy_diff.py` in 0.08s without a third Bazel invocation.
  - No C++ changes (PR #51376): **24s**.
- `DWYU (Depend on What You Use)`:
  - 2-file C++ change (PR #51377 vs. PR #50787): **1m53s** (down from **5m33s**, **66% faster**), analyzing 696 targets across the 2 modified packages in 96s instead of 15,729 targets across `//xla/...` in 202s.
  - No C++ changes (PR #51376 vs. PR #51241): **14s** (down from **5m18s**, **96% faster**).
- `Bazel Dependency Violations` (3 matrix jobs):
  - When build or `.bazelrc` files change (PR #51376 and PR #51377 vs. PR #50787): **3m19s-4m27s** (down from **6m28s-6m32s**, **32-49% faster**).
  - When no `BUILD`, `.bzl`, `WORKSPACE`, `MODULE.bazel`, or `.bazelrc` files change: skips `bazel cquery` in **~15s**.
- `Bazel Tags`: **1m04s-1m43s** (down from **3m18s** on PR #50787, **48-68% faster**).
- `Bazel Query`: **2m47s-3m12s** (down from **3m40s** on PR #50787, **13-24% faster**).

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add ScanRewriterTriton to the GPU compiler pipeline behind a flag.

head_commit.message:
Add the debug option `xla_gpu_experimental_enable_triton_scan` (default off). When it is set, `GpuCompiler` runs `ScanRewriterTriton` before `AssociativeScanRewriter`, so eligible associative `kScan` instructions become Triton scan fusions instead of reduce-window trees.

The rewriter only sets the fusion kind to `__triton`; the tiling is chosen later by `PriorityFusion`, `FusionBlockLevelRewriter` or the autotuner.

Eligible scans have rank 1 or 2 with the scan dimension last, and the rewriter does nothing on GPUs that Triton does not support. A tiled scan computes one row per block, so scans with a dimension of at least 32768 also need at least 64 rows (`kMinParallelElements`); otherwise the hierarchical scan of `AssociativeScanRewriter` is faster (crossover at 64 rows on H100 and 32 on B200). Shorter scans are faster with Triton at any batch size.

For a cumsum with an elementwise epilogue on f32[B, N], with B from 1 to 256 and N from 1024 to 262144, enabling the flag is never slower on H100 and B200. It is 1.05–2.9x (H100) and 1.06–2.8x (B200) faster for N < 32768, and up to 1.9x (H100) and 2.3x (B200) faster for N ≥ 32768 and B ≥ 64.

A top-p sampling mask (softmax, cumsum, compare and select) on f32[B, K] with B from 1 to 256 and K in {64, 128} compiles to a single Triton kernel: 1.3–1.5 µs instead of 3.3–4.5 µs on H100, and 2.5–3.1 µs instead of 5.9–8.4 µs on B200.

name: CI
display_title: Let PjRt OOM errors carry the reason why memory ran out.

head_commit.message:
Let PjRt OOM errors carry the reason why memory ran out.

`SetOomErrorWithPayload()` marks out-of-memory errors with an empty `pjrt.OOM` payload, so callers can tell that an operation ran out of memory, but not why: for example, whether the request was larger than the free memory or the free memory was too fragmented.

Add a required `OomReason` (`kOutOfMemory`, `kFragmentation` or `kUnknown`) to `SetOomErrorWithPayload()`, stored as the payload's value, and `GetOomErrorReason()` to read it back. `HasOomErrorPayload()` is unaffected.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1004508064

name: CI
display_title: [XLA] Memory-cost-aware latency hiding scheduler (kMemoryCost, aging, priced overlap)

head_commit.message:
[XLA] LHS: keep kMemoryCost off async starts and dones

Bottom-up, an async start looks like a pure releaser of the collective's
output, so kMemoryCost scored collective starts by bytes-per-cost and
reordered them. That is an overlap decision, not a memory one: it does not
change the peak by itself, but it perturbs the simulated timeline and can
flip downstream stall ties. On Qwen3-30B-A3B (GH200, 4-node AOT) one such
flip let the LM-head weight-gradient GEMM be used as overlap filler for a
tiny all-reduce after the backward loop, which kept the 5 GB logits gradient
live across the whole backward pass (+4.4 GB scheduler peak). Leaving async
starts and dones to the overlap rules restores the baseline schedule for
that model while keeping the rule's effect on compute releasers.

Adds AsyncStartsAreNotScored: with two independent all-gathers, the schedule
with the rule on must equal the one with it off.

display_title: PR #49450: [ROCm] Autotune the MFMA instruction size for Triton GEMMs

head_commit.message:
PR #49450: [ROCm] Autotune the MFMA instruction size for Triton GEMMs

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/49450

📝 Summary of Changes
Add `mfma_size` to the Triton GEMM config and autotune it on MFMA targets. MI300 default configs get `mfma_size: 16` variants. MI350 tries them only in exhaustive search.

🎯 Justification
The auto MFMA choice is often not the fastest on MI300.

🚀 Kind of Contribution:⚡️ Performance Improvement,

📊 Benchmark
  - MI300 wins: GPT-J 6B -12.9%, Flan-T5-L -9.7%, SDXL -6.5%, PaliGemma -5.5%.
Copybara import of the project:

--
263756c5777de795be80295c670e6b53a487dd56 by Aleksei Nurmukhametov <anurmukh@amd.com>:

[ROCm] Autotune the MFMA instruction size for Triton GEMMs

Triton picks the largest MFMA that fits the tile, which is not always
the fastest. Let the autotuner also try 16x16 MFMAs so it can pick
whichever is faster.

Tried by default on MI300 only. On MI350, it is limited to exhaustive
search. WMMA targets don't use MFMA.

Merging this change closes #49450

name: CI
display_title: Preserve `stack_frame_index` when embedding computations in `XlaBuilder`.

head_commit.message:
Preserve `stack_frame_index` when embedding computations in `XlaBuilder`.

`XlaBuilder::AddSubComputation` copied the embedded computation's
`HloComputationProto`s but dropped its `stack_frame_index`, leaving the
instructions' `stack_frame_id`s dangling. `HloModule::CanonicalizeStackFrameIds`
then reset them to 0, so source locations were lost for any computation built
via `ConvertMlirHloToHlo` and then embedded through `xla::Call`.

`XlaBuilder` now keeps a `StackFrames` table for imported computations:

-   `AddSubComputation` re-interns each imported frame (and its parent chain)
    into it, so identical frames are stored once, and rewrites the imported
    instructions' ids accordingly.
-   `BuildSubComputation` re-interns a child builder's table into its parent, only for entries that were imported with a stack frame index.
-   `Build()` / `BuildConstantSubGraph()` emit it as the module's
    `stack_frame_index`.
-   Ids set directly via `SetOpMetadata` (i.e. on the builder's own
    instructions, or on imported computations that carry no table) refer to a
    caller-owned table and are left untouched.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1000279666

name: CI
display_title: Explicitly set infinite timeout on CoordinationServiceAgent CallOptions.

head_commit.message:
Explicitly set infinite timeout on CoordinationServiceAgent CallOptions.

When `CoordinationServiceAgent` issues long-running or unbounded RPCs (`PollForErrorAsync`, `WatchTasksAsync`, `GetKeyValueAsync`, and `WaitAtBarrierAsync`), it previously left `tsl::CallOptions` at its default timeout of `0`. Because `tsl::RPCState::StartCall` only sets a deadline on `grpc::ClientContext` when `timeout_in_ms_ > 0`, a default-constructed `grpc::ClientContext` can inherit an ambient context deadline instead of having no deadline.

Explicitly set `call_opts->SetTimeout(absl::ToInt64Milliseconds(absl::InfiniteDuration()))` on these `CallOptions` so `gpr_time_from_millis` translates `INT64_MAX` to `gpr_inf_future` and overrides any ambient deadline.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1004475848

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Allow unaligned concatenate operands in Triton support checks.

`IsTritonSupportedConcatenate` rejected concatenates whose non-final operands
are not a multiple of 64 along the concatenate dimension. This pre-filter is
redundant: `VerifyConcatenateAlignment` in tile propagation already rejects
tilings whose tiles straddle operand boundaries, and smaller tile sizes can
still tile these concatenates. GEMM fusion keeps requiring 64-aligned
concatenate operands.

display_title: [XLA] Reverse kernel along reversed spatial dims in SimplifyConvToMultiply

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Reverse kernel along reversed spatial dims in SimplifyConvToMultiply

`AlgebraicSimplifierVisitor::SimplifyConvToMultiply` rewrites a convolution
whose spatial dimensions are all size 1 in either the kernel or the output into
a transpose, broadcast, multiply, and sum reduction. It previously ignored
`window_reversal` on the convolution window. When a contracted spatial dimension
has `window_reversal` set, the rewrite dropped the reversal and multiplied the
input by the unreversed kernel along that dimension. Reverse the kernel with
`MakeReverseHlo` along contracted spatial dimensions that have
`window_reversal` set before transposing and broadcasting.

[XLA] Reverse kernel along reversed spatial dims in SimplifyConvToMultiply

`AlgebraicSimplifierVisitor::SimplifyConvToMultiply` rewrites a convolution
whose spatial dimensions are all size 1 in either the kernel or the output into
a transpose, broadcast, multiply, and sum reduction. It previously ignored
`window_reversal` on the convolution window. When a contracted spatial dimension
has `window_reversal` set, the rewrite dropped the reversal and multiplied the
input by the unreversed kernel along that dimension. Reverse the kernel with
`MakeReverseHlo` along contracted spatial dimensions that have
`window_reversal` set before transposing and broadcasting.

display_title: Replace 32x32 type-conversion expansion in `LiteralBase::Convert` with two-stage chunked canonical conversion.

head_commit.message:
Replace 32x32 type-conversion expansion in `LiteralBase::Convert` with two-stage chunked canonical conversion.

`LiteralBase::Convert` (`ConvertSwitch` in `xla/literal.cc`) previously nested `ArrayTypeSwitch` inside `ArrayTypeSwitch`, instantiating `32 x 32 = 1,024` `ConvertBetweenNativeTypes<NativeSrcT, NativeDestT>` conversion loops (~464 KB in `literal.pic.o`, mostly from inlining software-emulated narrow float `F4..BF16` and sub-byte integer `S1..U4` conversions across >600 type pairs). Replace the 2D template expansion with two sequential 1D `ArrayTypeSwitch` stages operating on 512-element stack chunks through canonical 64-bit integer (`uint64_t`) and `float`/`double` intermediate buffers (`f32_buf` for `F4..F32` and `f64_buf` when `F64` is involved, using `Eigen::half_impl::narrow_to_float` round-to-odd when narrowing `double` or 32/64-bit integers to `F4..BF16` to avoid double-rounding at midpoints):

```
// Before: 32 x 32 = 1,024 instantiated loop bodies
ArrayTypeSwitch(src_type):
  ArrayTypeSwitch(dst_type):
    ConvertBetweenNativeTypes<SrcT, DstT>(src, dst)

// After: 32 + 32 = 64 1D chunk stages over L1-resident stack buffers
for each 512-element chunk:
  ArrayTypeSwitch(src_type): unpack SrcT -> canonical int_buf / f32_buf / f64_buf
  if (src_is_int != dst_is_int || src_uses_f64 != dst_uses_f64): bridge buffers
  ArrayTypeSwitch(dst_type): pack canonical int_buf / f32_buf / f64_buf -> DstT
```

Runtime and memory performance impact:
- Heap memory overhead is zero (`int_buf`, `f32_buf`, and `f64_buf` use 10 KB of fixed stack storage in L1 cache, and `Literal result` is allocated only after validating `IsComplexType(src) && !IsComplexType(dst)`).
- CPU runtime has no regression; each software-emulated narrow float or sub-byte integer element is converted once in a tight 1D loop rather than re-converting narrow floats to both `double` and `float` inside float-to-int saturation checks.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1004429027

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Lower atomic subf to fadd with a negated modifier

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Lower atomic subf to fadd with a negated modifier

`xla.atomic_rmw` can contain `subf(current, x)` after arithmetic
canonicalization. `GetAtomicModifierParameters` had no case for that form.
The CAS fallback handled those atomics, and jax-ml/jax#41467 reports the
resulting slowdown.

Handle `subf(current, x)` as `fadd(current, -x)` and add a `negated` flag
to `AtomicModifierParameters`. Emit the negate in the direct atomic and in
the vectorized yield. `subf(x, current)` and `subf(current, current)` still
use the CAS fallback.

Add tests for scalar f32, widened bf16, the swapped case, and the Hopper
vectorization path. `//xla/codegen/emitters/transforms/tests:tests` passes
25/25.

name: CI
display_title: Support `UnpinnedHostMemorySpace` in PJRT GPU.

head_commit.message:
Support `UnpinnedHostMemorySpace` in PJRT GPU.

PJRT GPU devices previously only attached device HBM and pinned host memory spaces, preventing callers from allocating, importing, or transferring buffers in `UnpinnedHostMemorySpace`.

Attach `UnpinnedHostMemorySpace` to each addressable GPU device and register `UnpinnedHostMemorySpace::kKindId` in `StreamExecutorGpuTopologyDescription`. In `PjRtStreamExecutorRawClient`, delegate buffer allocation, foreign memory import, and event creation for `UnpinnedHostMemorySpace` to `CpuRawBuffer` and `CpuEvent`, and enable zero-copy host buffer import on GPU for unpinned host memory. Update `PjRtStreamExecutorRawBuffer` copy paths to route transfers targeting `UnpinnedHostMemorySpace` through host memory copies rather than intra-client StreamExecutor device transfers.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1005173487

name: CI
display_title: Add HloComputation::HasCalledComputations() to skip leaf computation scans.

head_commit.message:
Add HloComputation::HasCalledComputations() to skip leaf computation scans.

Post-fusion XLA modules contain thousands of leaf fusion and reducer
computations that call no subcomputations, yet `CallGraph::Build`, `HloDCE`,
`MakeComputationPostOrder`, `RemoveUnusedComputations`,
`MakeEmbeddedComputationsList`, and `CollectivePipeliner` scan every
instruction in leaf computations looking for callees or `while` loops.

Expose `HloComputation::HasCalledComputations()` (backed by the existing
`callee_computations_` map) and combine it with
`HloInstruction::MightHaveCalledComputations()` on `instructions_with_info()`
to skip leaf computations in O(1) and skip non-calling opcodes without
chasing instruction pointers.

Previously, `PjRtArray::CopySinglePjRtBuffer` rejected `ArrayCopySemantics::kDonateInput` when copying across different memory kinds with an `Unimplemented` error, left the source array's `PjRtBuffer` pointer intact when donating on the same device and memory kind, and did not call `PjRtBuffer::Delete()` on the source buffer when donating across devices or memory spaces. In addition, several `PjRtArray` methods assumed elements of `pjrt_buffers_` were non-null even after cross-device donation set `pjrt_buffers_[index] = nullptr`.

Allow `ArrayCopySemantics::kDonateInput` across different memory spaces in `PjRtArray::CopySinglePjRtBuffer` by deleting and clearing the source `PjRtBuffer` after `CopyToMemorySpace` initiates the transfer, and move `pjrt_buffers_[index]` when donating on the same device and memory kind so the source `PjRtArray` is marked deleted. Guard against null donated buffer slots in `CopySinglePjRtBuffer`, `CopyImpl`, `CopyToHostBuffer`, `GetReadyFuture`, and debug checks in `pjrt_layout`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1004877589

head_commit.message:
Allow 256-bit vectorization in Triton for NVIDIA Blackwell (`sm_100+`).

Permit vector sizes up to 256 bits in `pickDescriptorLoadStoreLayout`
(`Coalesce.cpp`) and `getMaxElementsPerThread` (`Utility.cpp`) when targeting
NVIDIA architectures with compute capability `>= 100`. Previous logic capped
vectorization and descriptor tile layouts at 128 bits, preventing 256-bit
vectorized global loads/stores and optimal 2D TMA descriptor generation on
Blackwell.

On B200 (Triton TMA transpose path, device time on `bf16` large 2D transposes):

- K255: 191 -> 169 µs
- K127: 99 -> 87 µs
- K37: 29.7 -> 27.5 µs

display_title: Speed up single-threaded `GetMatchingPaths` and `FileSystem::IsDirectory`.

head_commit.message:
Speed up single-threaded `GetMatchingPaths` and `FileSystem::IsDirectory`.

In `GetMatchingPaths`, each `parent` directory in the queue has already been matched at previous levels, so we only need to match each `child` entry against the current segment's basename (`base_pattern`) rather than joining `parent` and `child` and re-matching the full path prefix. This avoids both re-evaluating earlier path components in `Match` and allocating joined path strings for non-matching entries.

Additionally, skip `GetChildren` when `base_pattern` contains no glob characters, avoid redundant `FileExists` calls on entries returned by `GetChildren`, reuse the `children` vector across iterations, and remove the redundant `FileExists` check before `Stat` in `FileSystem::IsDirectory`.

name: CI
display_title: Add HloComputation::HasCalledComputations() to skip leaf computation scans.

head_commit.message:
Add HloComputation::HasCalledComputations() to skip leaf computation scans.

Post-fusion XLA modules contain thousands of leaf fusion and reducer
computations that call no subcomputations, yet `CallGraph::Build`, `HloDCE`,
`MakeComputationPostOrder`, `RemoveUnusedComputations`,
`MakeEmbeddedComputationsList`, and `CollectivePipeliner` scan every
instruction in leaf computations looking for callees or `while` loops.

Expose `HloComputation::HasCalledComputations()` (backed by the existing
`callee_computations_` map) and combine it with
`HloInstruction::MightHaveCalledComputations()` on `instructions_with_info()`
to skip leaf computations in O(1) and skip non-calling opcodes without
chasing instruction pointers.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1005024627

name: CI
display_title: Add DeserializeLoadedExecutable RPC to IFRT Proxy

head_commit.message:
Add DeserializeLoadedExecutable RPC to IFRT Proxy

Adds protocol version 26 and a new IfrtRequest/IfrtResponse pair so a client
can load a serialized executable on the server backend.

Client: Compiler::DeserializeLoadedExecutable uploads the bytes through the
host buffer store, sends the request, and builds the executable from the
CompileResponse. It returns Unimplemented if the server is older than
version 26, and rejects host callbacks.

Server: IfrtBackend handles the request on the compile thread pool, waits for
the uploaded bytes, calls the default Compiler, and returns the same
CompileResponse as Compile. The Compile response code is now shared.

The previous Unimplemented error cited an unstable serialization format. That is
not a concern here: the proxy never reads the bytes and sends them unchanged.
The server backend that loads them checks that they match its own runtime and
returns an error status if they do not. The same compatibility rule applies to
any IFRT client that loads a serialized executable.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1000592516

[XLA] Seed callee memory pressure trackers from the caller

ModulePressureState::ResetPressureStates built the tracker of every called
computation from the caller's live buffer set, looking up each live buffer.

vector and live set. It takes the caller's memory usage as the initial
pressure, which is what Reset() computes from the set. The finished pressure
state moves into the state map. Schedules are unchanged.

head_commit.message:
PR #50858: [PJRT:GPU] Align topology and client platform versions

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50858

### :pencil: Summary of Changes

Make GPU topology `platform_version()` report the software version, such as `cuda 13040`, consistently with the GPU client. Share the existing version formatter and preserve GPU model names in `device_kind()` and serialized topology metadata. This addresses failure in JAX which depends on the topology `platform_version` reporting the CUDA version rather than device name.

The intent from the comments appears to be that `platform_version` from the compile client should be the CUDA version rather than the device name \[1\], but this isn't how it is actually populated \[2\]:

\[1\] https://github.com/openxla/xla/blob/main/xla/pjrt/pjrt_client.h#L614-L616

```
      // Returns a string containing human-readable, platform-specific version info
   // (e.g. the CUDA version on GPU or libtpu version on Cloud TPU).
   virtual absl::string_view platform_version() const = 0;
```

\[2\] https://github.com/openxla/xla/blob/main/xla/pjrt/distributed/topology_util.cc#L422-L424

```
     if (gpu_topology.platform_version().empty()) {
    gpu_topology.set_platform_version(device.name());
  }
```

### :dart: Justification

GPU compile-only clients inherit their platform version from the topology, which previously returned the device model. This fixes inconsistent metadata between runtime and compile-only clients, benefiting JAX/XLA AOT and deviceless compilation workflows.

display_title: Return sorted results from Env::GetMatchingPaths for every file system.

head_commit.message:
Return sorted results from Env::GetMatchingPaths for every file system.

`GetMatchingPaths` returned paths in whatever order the file system produced. The POSIX and Windows file systems used directory-listing order, which varies by file system and, with `multithreaded=true`, by thread scheduling. `EmbedFileSystem` used hash-map order, while `GcsFileSystem` and `RamFileSystem` already returned sorted paths. Code that indexes into the results, for example to number devices, therefore behaved differently across machines.

`Env::GetMatchingPaths` now guarantees ascending lexicographic order, sorting the results only when the file system didn't already. The built-in file systems that didn't sort now do as well, so direct `FileSystem::GetMatchingPaths` callers also get sorted results.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Keep the physical layout of the dot result in SplitkRewriter.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Keep the physical layout of the dot result in SplitkRewriter.

`SplitkRewriter` created the split-K dot with the default layout, regardless of the layout of the original dot result, and then forced the layout of the original dot result onto the split-K reduction. Whenever layout assignment had given the dot a non-default result layout (for example, `bf16[1536,256]{0,1}` for a dot whose result is transposed before it is consumed), the split-K reduction therefore also had to transpose its operand (`f32[8,1536,256]{2,1,0}` to `f32[1536,256]{0,1}`), which turns the cheap split-K reduction into a poorly coalesced transposing reduction.

Give the split-K dot the physical layout of the original dot result with the split-K dimension as the most major dimension instead, so that the reduction over the split-K dimension only sums contiguous slices of its operand. Triton emits the GEMM tiles in the requested layout at no extra cost. The result is numerically identical.

Add an end-to-end test that merges two quantized projections of the same activations (q and kv projections of an attention block), splits K, and checks that all split-K reductions read and write their operands in the default layout.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1004999728

display_title: Speed up single-threaded `GetMatchingPaths` and `FileSystem::IsDirectory`.

head_commit.message:
Speed up single-threaded `GetMatchingPaths` and `FileSystem::IsDirectory`.

In `GetMatchingPaths`, each `parent` directory in the queue has already been matched at previous levels, so we only need to match each `child` entry against the current segment's basename (`base_pattern`) rather than joining `parent` and `child` and re-matching the full path prefix. This avoids both re-evaluating earlier path components in `Match` and allocating joined path strings for non-matching entries.

Additionally, skip `GetChildren` when `base_pattern` contains no glob characters, avoid redundant `FileExists` calls on entries returned by `GetChildren`, reuse the `children` vector across iterations, and remove the redundant `FileExists` check before `Stat` in `FileSystem::IsDirectory`.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Remove repeated work from the latency hiding scheduler

ShouldDelaySendHostDone looked up the send node of a send-done on every
comparison of the ready set. It also asked the latency estimator for the
send to send-done latency each time. The schedule graph now stores both when
it is built, next to the edge latencies.

on the two instructions only. AIsBetterThanB recomputed
resource_constrained for the running best candidate on every comparison.
The value is now kept for one search, since the resource maps only change
when a node is scheduled. BufferInfoTracker walked every shape index of
every operand use through HloAliasAnalysis::ComputeBuffersAt. It now keeps
one buffer list per instruction of the computation it walks.
MemoryPressureTracker::live_buffers() returns a const reference and
ModulePressureState moves the pressure state into its map. Schedules are
unchanged.

display_title: [XLA:CPU][oneDNN] Fix data race in OneDnnThreadPool::parallel_for()

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU][oneDNN] Fix data race in OneDnnThreadPool::parallel_for()

Fixes data race in oneDnnThreadPool::parallel_for() for both sync and async cases, when we're running in multi-threaded mode. The issue was caused by the fact, that oneDnnThreadPool::get_in_parallel() was always returning false. Because of that, when some oneDNN kernels started inner parallel_for(), those functions were unable to see that they were running inside of a thread already. This caused them to overwrite done_event_ from outer parallel_for().

The fix implements needed checks to satisfy oneDNN contract, which is stated in `src/common/dnnl_thread.hpp`:
Since oneDNN does not allow nested parallelism, inside a parallel region the number of available threads is 1.

display_title: PR #50858: [PJRT:GPU] Align topology and client platform versions

head_commit.message:
PR #50858: [PJRT:GPU] Align topology and client platform versions

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50858

### :pencil: Summary of Changes

Make GPU topology `platform_version()` report the software version, such as `cuda 13040`, consistently with the GPU client. Share the existing version formatter and preserve GPU model names in `device_kind()` and serialized topology metadata. This addresses failure in JAX which depends on the topology `platform_version` reporting the CUDA version rather than device name.

The intent from the comments appears to be that `platform_version` from the compile client should be the CUDA version rather than the device name \[1\], but this isn't how it is actually populated \[2\]:

\[1\] https://github.com/openxla/xla/blob/main/xla/pjrt/pjrt_client.h#L614-L616

display_title: [ROCm] Fall back to an unfused FP8 conversion when hipBLASLt has no kernel

head_commit.message:
[ROCm] Fall back to an unfused FP8 conversion when hipBLASLt has no kernel

Motivation:
hipBLASLt kernel coverage for FP8 outputs differs between GPUs and library
releases. Instead of failing to compile with "No supported configs found",
run such a GEMM with a wider output and convert it to FP8 separately.

Details:
- When hipBLASLt returns no algorithm for an FP8-output GEMM,
  HipblasLtBackend offers the algorithms of a wider-output copy, marked by
  the new GemmKey.unfuse_fp8_output. ApplyConfig rewrites the call into
  that GEMM plus a loop fusion for the D scale, saturating clamp and
  conversion.
- Fused kernels are never displaced, and HIPBLASLT_FISSION gets the
  fallback through its inner backend.

Test Plan:
hipblaslt_test, fission_backend_test and gemm_rewriter_fp8_test pass on
gfx950.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Keep the latency hiding scheduler's ready set scan off the HloInstruction

The overlap limit test of the ready set scan dereferenced the HloInstruction
of every examined node to ask whether it calls a computation synchronously.
The async done tie break of the comparator and the host send done rule
resolved starts through the instruction and the node map on every
comparison. Both facts are fixed while the schedule graph exists, so the
graph now stores them on the node and its Rare entry when it is built.
Schedules are unchanged.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Hoist dynamic slice offsets out of concatenate regions

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Hoist dynamic slice offsets out of concatenate regions

Let me know if this isn't the correct fix, but when enabling dynamic-slices, we found that a concatenate could concatenate the same dynamic-slice result as multiple operands. In tiling, concatenate branches are hoisting barriers, so a
dynamic slice that is reachable from several branches gets its offsets tiled in
each of them. However, `rt_symbol_to_tiled_hlo` maps each runtime variable to a
single tiled instruction (the one from the first branch), and the emitter uses
it in all branches, where it does not dominate its uses:

  error: operand #1 does not dominate this use

Runtime variables are scalars that do not depend on the tile, so hoist them out
of conditional regions too.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Keep the physical layout of the dot result in SplitkRewriter.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Keep the physical layout of the dot result in SplitkRewriter.

`SplitkRewriter` created the split-K dot with the default layout, regardless of the layout of the original dot result, and then forced the layout of the original dot result onto the split-K reduction. Whenever layout assignment had given the dot a non-default result layout (for example, `bf16[1536,256]{0,1}` for a dot whose result is transposed before it is consumed), the split-K reduction therefore also had to transpose its operand (`f32[8,1536,256]{2,1,0}` to `f32[1536,256]{0,1}`), which turns the cheap split-K reduction into a poorly coalesced transposing reduction.

Give the split-K dot the physical layout of the original dot result with the split-K dimension as the most major dimension instead, so that the reduction over the split-K dimension only sums contiguous slices of its operand. Triton emits the GEMM tiles in the requested layout at no extra cost. The result is numerically identical.

Add an end-to-end test that merges two quantized projections of the same activations (q and kv projections of an attention block), splits K, and checks that all split-K reductions read and write their operands in the default layout.

head_commit.message:
PR #126327: Introduce tf.distribute.AutoStrategy

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/pull/126327

# Introduce `tf.distribute.AutoStrategy`

## Description
This pull request introduces the "Zero-Code" Distributed Training Optimizer feature: `tf.distribute.AutoStrategy`.

Currently, developers have to manually probe their hardware environments or manage boilerplate conditionals in their training scripts to select the appropriate distribution strategy (`MirroredStrategy`, `TPUStrategy`, `OneDeviceStrategy`, etc.).

`AutoStrategy` is a dynamic factory API that automatically resolves and initializes the optimal strategy for the user based on the environment and available hardware.

### Key Changes
- **New API:** Added `tf.distribute.AutoStrategy()` exposed via `@tf_export`.
- **Heuristics Engine:**
  - Detects `TF_CONFIG` to return `MultiWorkerMirroredStrategy` for distributed clusters.
  - Automatically initializes and routes to `TPUStrategy` if TPUs are present via `tf.config.list_logical_devices`.
  - Discovers multiple local GPUs and returns `MirroredStrategy`.
  - Safely falls back to `OneDeviceStrategy` (GPU or CPU) in resource-constrained environments.
- **Testing:** Added robust unit tests in `auto_strategy_test.py` to ensure correct factory resolutions across mocked hardware environments.
- **Build integration:** Updated the Python bazel `BUILD` targets to include the new strategy module seamlessly.

## Motivation and Context
Simplifies the boilerplate MLOps setup required for distributed machine learning in TensorFlow, especially when moving model code from a single-GPU dev environment to a TPU or multi-worker production cluster. This strongly aligns with TensorFlow's goal of offering an enterprise-ready, out-of-the-box deployment experience.

## How Has This Been Tested?
- [x] Unit tests covering CPU fallback and multi-worker `TF_CONFIG` discovery (`bazel test //tensorflow/python/distribute:auto_strategy_test`)
- [x] Linting and syntax checks verified against `tf_py_strict_test`.

## Types of changes
- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)

display_title: [XLA:CPU][oneDNN] Fix data race in OneDnnThreadPool::parallel_for()

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU][oneDNN] Fix data race in OneDnnThreadPool::parallel_for()

Fixes data race in oneDnnThreadPool::parallel_for() for both sync and async cases, when we're running in multi-threaded mode. The issue was caused by the fact, that oneDnnThreadPool::get_in_parallel() was always returning false. Because of that, when some oneDNN kernels started inner parallel_for(), those functions were unable to see that they were running inside of a thread already. This caused them to overwrite done_event_ from outer parallel_for().

The fix implements needed checks to satisfy oneDNN contract, which is stated in `src/common/dnnl_thread.hpp`:
Since oneDNN does not allow nested parallelism, inside a parallel region the number of available threads is 1.

display_title: Speed up single-threaded `GetMatchingPaths` and `FileSystem::IsDirectory`.

head_commit.message:
Speed up single-threaded `GetMatchingPaths` and `FileSystem::IsDirectory`.

In `GetMatchingPaths`, each `parent` directory in the queue has already been matched at previous levels, so we only need to match each `child` entry against the current segment's basename (`base_pattern`) rather than joining `parent` and `child` and re-matching the full path prefix. This avoids both re-evaluating earlier path components in `Match` and allocating joined path strings for non-matching entries.

Additionally, skip `GetChildren` when `base_pattern` contains no glob characters, avoid redundant `FileExists` calls on entries returned by `GetChildren`, reuse the `children` vector across iterations, and remove the redundant `FileExists` check before `Stat` in `FileSystem::IsDirectory`.

1. Only the RHS producer generated non-trivial code and the LHS had a small non-contracting dimension (`< 128`), or
2. Neither operand generated code and the LHS had a smaller non-contracting dimension than the RHS (with LHS `< 128`).

When both the LHS and RHS producers of a dot in a Triton GEMM fusion generated code—for example, when the LHS has an activation/scale prologue (`convert` + `broadcast` + `multiply`) with a smaller non-contracting dimension (`M`) and the RHS has a weight dequantization prologue (`convert`) with a much larger non-contracting dimension (`N`)—`MaybeSwapOperands` returned early without swapping. Keeping the larger dimension on the RHS (`N`) prevented Triton from selecting tile shapes with a larger LHS tile and smaller RHS tile, causing autotuning to fall back to `CUBLASLT_FISSION` (unnesting the weight conversion into a separate memory-bound kernel that materializes the converted weights to global memory).

Update `MaybeSwapOperands` in `xla/backends/gpu/transforms/gemm_fusion_swap_operands.cc` so that when both operands generate code, we compare their non-contracting dimensions directly and swap them whenever the LHS non-contracting dimension is strictly smaller than the RHS non-contracting dimension (`lhs_noncontracting_size < rhs_noncontracting_size`). Add unit tests in `xla/backends/gpu/transforms/gemm_fusion_swap_operands_test.cc` covering both-code-generating, single-code-generating, and neither-code-generating cases.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Keep the physical layout of the dot result in SplitkRewriter.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Keep the physical layout of the dot result in SplitkRewriter.

`SplitkRewriter` created the split-K dot with the default layout, regardless of the layout of the original dot result, and then forced the layout of the original dot result onto the split-K reduction. Whenever layout assignment had given the dot a non-default result layout (for example, `bf16[1536,256]{0,1}` for a dot whose result is transposed before it is consumed), the split-K reduction therefore also had to transpose its operand (`f32[8,1536,256]{2,1,0}` to `f32[1536,256]{0,1}`), which turns the cheap split-K reduction into a poorly coalesced transposing reduction.

Give the split-K dot the physical layout of the original dot result with the split-K dimension as the most major dimension instead, so that the reduction over the split-K dimension only sums contiguous slices of its operand. Triton emits the GEMM tiles in the requested layout at no extra cost. The result is numerically identical.

Add an end-to-end test that merges two quantized projections of the same activations (q and kv projections of an attention block), splits K, and checks that all split-K reductions read and write their operands in the default layout.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1003885965

display_title: [XLA] Memoize the stack frame index per call stack on StableHLO to HLO export

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Memoize the stack frame index per call stack on StableHLO to HLO export

StackFrameIndexBuilder::AddCallStackAndGetFirstFrameId reindexed the whole
call stack of every exported op. Call stack locations are uniqued and shared
by all ops with the same stack frame, so after the first op nothing is
inserted. Walk each location once, skipping the leading op name wrappers,
and memoize the innermost frame id of every (location, parent frame) pair.
A repeated call stack, a shared caller or the callee stack of an inlined op
is then one hash lookup.
The function returns the frame id; the unused result fields are gone. The
produced StackFrameIndexProto and stack_frame_ids are unchanged.

name: CI
display_title: Fix RAFT CUDA intrinsics compatibility patch for Clang 21 and 22.

head_commit.message:
Fix RAFT CUDA intrinsics compatibility patch for Clang 21 and 22.

On 64-bit Linux (LP64), `uint64_t` aliases `unsigned long`, so instantiating RAFT's `select_warpsort.cuh` for `uint64_t` calls `__ldcs(const unsigned long*)`. Clang 21 and 22 added `__ldcg`, `__ldcs`, `__ldcv`, and `__stwt` (https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/144851), but omitted the `unsigned long` overloads for `__ldcg`, `__ldcs`, and `__ldcv` and both `long` and `unsigned long` overloads for `__stwt` until Clang 23.

Extend the compatibility header guard to `__clang_major__ < 23`. For Clang 21 and 22, define only the missing `unsigned long` overloads for `cg`, `cs`, and `cv` loads and the `long` and `unsigned long` overloads for `wt` stores to avoid redefinition conflicts with Clang's built-in intrinsics, while retaining the full `ca` and `lu` load families and `cg`, `cs`, and `wb` store families added in Clang 23.

Related:
- [jaxlib with conda-forge PR-359](https://github.com/conda-forge/jaxlib-feedstock/pull/359)
- [XLA #31367](https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/31367)
- [LLVM #190021](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/190021)

display_title: Speed up single-threaded `GetMatchingPaths` and `FileSystem::IsDirectory`.

head_commit.message:
Speed up single-threaded `GetMatchingPaths` and `FileSystem::IsDirectory`.

In `GetMatchingPaths`, each `parent` directory in the queue has already been matched at previous levels, so we only need to match each `child` entry against the current segment's basename (`base_pattern`) rather than joining `parent` and `child` and re-matching the full path prefix. This avoids both re-evaluating earlier path components in `Match` and allocating joined path strings for non-matching entries.

Additionally, skip `GetChildren` when `base_pattern` contains no glob characters, avoid redundant `FileExists` calls on entries returned by `GetChildren`, reuse the `children` vector across iterations, and remove the redundant `FileExists` check before `Stat` in `FileSystem::IsDirectory`.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Swap GEMM operands when both generate code and RHS is larger.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Swap GEMM operands when both generate code and RHS is larger.

Previously, `GemmFusionSwapOperands` only swapped GEMM operands when:
1. Only the RHS producer generated non-trivial code and the LHS had a small non-contracting dimension (`< 128`), or
2. Neither operand generated code and the LHS had a smaller non-contracting dimension than the RHS (with LHS `< 128`).

When both the LHS and RHS producers of a dot in a Triton GEMM fusion generated code—for example, when the LHS has an activation/scale prologue (`convert` + `broadcast` + `multiply`) with a smaller non-contracting dimension (`M`) and the RHS has a weight dequantization prologue (`convert`) with a much larger non-contracting dimension (`N`)—`MaybeSwapOperands` returned early without swapping. Keeping the larger dimension on the RHS (`N`) prevented Triton from selecting tile shapes with a larger LHS tile and smaller RHS tile, causing autotuning to fall back to `CUBLASLT_FISSION` (unnesting the weight conversion into a separate memory-bound kernel that materializes the converted weights to global memory).

Update `MaybeSwapOperands` in `xla/backends/gpu/transforms/gemm_fusion_swap_operands.cc` so that when both operands generate code, we compare their non-contracting dimensions directly and swap them whenever the LHS non-contracting dimension is strictly smaller than the RHS non-contracting dimension (`lhs_noncontracting_size < rhs_noncontracting_size`). Add unit tests in `xla/backends/gpu/transforms/gemm_fusion_swap_operands_test.cc` covering both-code-generating, single-code-generating, and neither-code-generating cases.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1003355666

display_title: Fix RAFT CUDA intrinsics compatibility patch for Clang 21 and 22.

head_commit.message:
Fix RAFT CUDA intrinsics compatibility patch for Clang 21 and 22.

On 64-bit Linux (LP64), `uint64_t` aliases `unsigned long`, so instantiating RAFT's `select_warpsort.cuh` for `uint64_t` calls `__ldcs(const unsigned long*)`. Clang 21 and 22 added `__ldcg`, `__ldcs`, `__ldcv`, and `__stwt` (https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/144851), but omitted the `unsigned long` overloads for `__ldcg`, `__ldcs`, and `__ldcv` and both `long` and `unsigned long` overloads for `__stwt` until Clang 23.

Extend the compatibility header guard to `__clang_major__ < 23`. For Clang 21 and 22, define only the missing `unsigned long` overloads for `cg`, `cs`, and `cv` loads and the `long` and `unsigned long` overloads for `wt` stores to avoid redefinition conflicts with Clang's built-in intrinsics, while retaining the full `ca` and `lu` load families and `cg`, `cs`, and `wb` store families added in Clang 23.

Related:
- [jaxlib with conda-forge PR-359](https://github.com/conda-forge/jaxlib-feedstock/pull/359)
- [XLA #31367](https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/31367)
- [LLVM #190021](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/190021)

display_title: [XLA:CPU][oneDNN] Fix data race in OneDnnThreadPool::parallel_for()

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU][oneDNN] Fix data race in OneDnnThreadPool ::parallel_for()

Fixes data race in oneDnnThreadPool::parallel_for() for both sync and async cases, when we're running in multi-threaded mode. The issue was caused by the fact, that oneDnnThreadPool::get_in_parallel() was always returning false. Because of that, when some oneDNN kernels started inner parallel_for(), those functions were unable to see that they were running inside of a thread already. This caused them to overwrite done_event_ from outer parallel_for().

The fix implements needed checks to satisfy oneDNN contract, which is stated in `src/common/dnnl_thread.hpp`:
Since oneDNN does not allow nested parallelism, inside a parallel region the number of available threads is 1.

display_title: PR #49816: [XLA:GPU] Match FP8 dequantization normalized to f32 in GemmRewriter

head_commit.message:
PR #49816: [XLA:GPU] Match FP8 dequantization normalized to f32 in GemmRewriter

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/49816

## Summary

FloatNormalization can widen a bf16 dequantization (multiply or divide by scale) to f32, producing `convert(bf16_param) -> f32` before the dot. `MatchFp8Param` now looks through that convert so GemmRewriter still captures the original scale and fuses the FP8 GEMM.

- The scale is converted to f32 before computing the reciprocal (for the divide path) to avoid precision loss.
- Only floating-point, non-FP8 scales are matched.

## Test plan

- Existing `gemm_rewriter_fp8_test` tests extended with `ConvertedF32` variants that cover the widened-scale pattern for both multiply and divide paths.
- `F32ScaleNotConverted` test verifies that an f32 scale (which doesn't need widening) still matches correctly.
Copybara import of the project:

--

display_title: Return sorted results from Env::GetMatchingPaths for every file system.

head_commit.message:
Return sorted results from Env::GetMatchingPaths for every file system.

`GetMatchingPaths` returned paths in whatever order the file system produced. The POSIX and Windows file systems used directory-listing order, which varies by file system and, with `multithreaded=true`, by thread scheduling. `EmbedFileSystem` used hash-map order, while `GcsFileSystem` and `RamFileSystem` already returned sorted paths. Code that indexes into the results, for example to number devices, therefore behaved differently across machines.

`Env::GetMatchingPaths` now guarantees ascending lexicographic order, sorting the results only when the file system didn't already. The built-in file systems that didn't sort now do as well, so direct `FileSystem::GetMatchingPaths` callers also get sorted results.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add ScanRewriterTriton to the GPU compiler pipeline behind a flag.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add ScanRewriterTriton to the GPU compiler pipeline behind a flag.

Add the debug option `xla_gpu_experimental_enable_triton_scan` (default off). When it is set, `GpuCompiler` runs `ScanRewriterTriton` in `OptimizeHloPostLayoutAssignment` before `AssociativeScanRewriter`, so eligible associative `kScan` instructions become Triton scan fusions instead of reduce-window trees.

The rewriter only sets the fusion kind to `__triton`; the tiling is chosen later by `PriorityFusion`, `FusionBlockLevelRewriter` or the autotuner.

`GpuCompiler` only adds the rewriter on GPUs that Triton supports. A tiled scan computes one row per block, so scans with a dimension of at least 32768 also need at least 64 rows (`kMinRowsForLongScan`); otherwise the hierarchical scan of `AssociativeScanRewriter` is faster (crossover at 64 rows on H100 and 32 on B200). Shorter scans are faster with Triton at any batch size.

`CanTritonHandleScan` now rejects scans over any dimension other than the last one, for which the tiled Triton scan computes wrong results.

For a cumsum with an elementwise epilogue on f32[B, N], with B from 1 to 256 and N from 1024 to 262144, enabling the flag is never slower on H100 and B200. It is 1.05–2.9x (H100) and 1.06–2.8x (B200) faster for N < 32768, and up to 1.9x (H100) and 2.3x (B200) faster for N ≥ 32768 and B ≥ 64.

A top-p sampling mask (softmax, cumsum, compare and select) on f32[B, K] with B from 1 to 256 and K in {64, 128} compiles to a single Triton kernel: 1.3–1.5 µs instead of 3.3–4.5 µs on H100, and 2.5–3.1 µs instead of 5.9–8.4 µs on B200.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 982293610

display_title: Speed up Clang-Tidy, DWYU, and query CI workflows

head_commit.message:
Speed up Clang-Tidy, DWYU, and query CI workflows

The Clang-Tidy, DWYU, and Bazel query/lint workflows in GitHub Actions currently repeat full-repository analysis or do unnecessary work on every pull request:

1. In `clang_tidy.yml` and `run_clang_tidy.sh`, the workflow invokes `./configure.py` (which is meant for local developer setups rather than CI) and writes `build:cuda` and `test --test_env` flags into `xla_configure.bazelrc` that cause `bazel build` to discard the `bazel cquery` analysis cache. name: CI
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add ScanRewriterTriton to the GPU compiler pipeline behind a flag.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add ScanRewriterTriton to the GPU compiler pipeline behind a flag.

Add the debug option `xla_gpu_experimental_enable_triton_scan` (default off). When it is set, `GpuCompiler` runs `ScanRewriterTriton` in `OptimizeHloPostLayoutAssignment` before `AssociativeScanRewriter`, so eligible associative `kScan` instructions become Triton scan fusions instead of reduce-window trees.

The rewriter only sets the fusion kind to `__triton`; the tiling is chosen later by `PriorityFusion`, `FusionBlockLevelRewriter` or the autotuner.

`GpuCompiler` only adds the rewriter on GPUs that Triton supports. A tiled scan computes one row per block, so scans with a dimension of at least 32768 also need at least 64 rows (`kMinRowsForLongScan`); otherwise the hierarchical scan of `AssociativeScanRewriter` is faster (crossover at 64 rows on H100 and 32 on B200). Shorter scans are faster with Triton at any batch size.

`CanTritonHandleScan` now rejects scans over any dimension other than the last one, for which the tiled Triton scan computes wrong results.

For a cumsum with an elementwise epilogue on f32[B, N], with B from 1 to 256 and N from 1024 to 262144, enabling the flag is never slower on H100 and B200. It is 1.05–2.9x (H100) and 1.06–2.8x (B200) faster for N < 32768, and up to 1.9x (H100) and 2.3x (B200) faster for N ≥ 32768 and B ≥ 64.

A top-p sampling mask (softmax, cumsum, compare and select) on f32[B, K] with B from 1 to 256 and K in {64, 128} compiles to a single Triton kernel: 1.3–1.5 µs instead of 3.3–4.5 µs on H100, and 2.5–3.1 µs instead of 5.9–8.4 µs on B200.

name: CI
display_title: [XLA] Run MemorySpacePropagation without a whole module dataflow analysis

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Run MemorySpacePropagation without a whole module dataflow analysis

MemorySpacePropagation::Run built an HloDataflowAnalysis of the whole module
to read one value per fusion operand and output leaf. Inside a fusion
computation a value flows only through get-tuple-element, tuple,
add-dependency, domain, optimization-barrier and the nested elements of copy,
so Run now computes the positions and fusion uses it needs from the fusion
computation itself. It builds the analysis only when a fusion computation
holds a call, control flow or an asynchronous operation. Both paths visit
the same positions and fusion uses, so the resulting HLO is unchanged.
